# Workflow policy templates

Reusable defaults for new projects, not a record of production observations or human approvals.
A built-in policy states its default enforcement explicitly. Private projects may copy and govern their own rules; no project history is included here.

Policy pack v1.0: 51 reusable rules.

## Design principles

### R-DEN-001 — One primary message per frame: introduce entities progressively on their spoken cue; avoid dense node graphs, simultaneous animations, tiny labels and excess connectors.

- **Check:** tool `legibility:check (density)`; rubric dimensions: LEG-DENSITY, CRE-ONE-MESSAGE
- **Default:** enforced
  - **Never:** Show the whole system at once
  - **Never:** Animate several groups simultaneously
  - **Always:** Reveal one idea per spoken cue
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_density_limit`

### R-DES-001 — Bookends follow the project's approved typography, palette, visual hierarchy and required supplied marks.

- **Check:** reviewer cases; rubric dimensions: DES-BOOKENDS
- **Default:** enforced
  - **Never:** Busy bookends with competing elements
  - **Never:** Small bookend text
  - **Never:** Omit a supplied mark required by the approved brief
  - **Always:** Use the approved title treatment and supplied marks

### R-DES-003 — Logos and marks are the supplied files, scaled uniformly; never regenerated, morphed or deformed.

- **Check:** tool `design:compliance`; rubric dimensions: DES-LOGO
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_design_compliance_flags_font_logo_palette`

### R-DES-004 — Reuse techniques without importing unapproved fonts, palettes, UI, counters or architecture claims.

- **Check:** tool `design:compliance (prohibited patterns)`; rubric dimensions: DES-PROHIBITED
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_design_compliance_flags_font_logo_palette`

## Creative and narrative preferences

### R-NAR-001 — Frame the story as the platform helping the customer's experts solve their business problems (the customer is the protagonist).

- **Check:** reviewer cases; rubric dimensions: NAR-PERSPECTIVE
- **Default:** enforced
  - **Never:** A feature tour without a business problem
  - **Always:** Name whose problem is solved and how

### R-NAR-002 — The film is one connected story: every scene connects to the one before and after; nothing is introduced before the viewer is ready.

- **Check:** reviewer cases; rubric dimensions: NAR-CONNECTION, NAR-CLARITY
- **Default:** enforced
  - **Never:** A scene that repeats information without adding value
  - **Never:** A concept introduced before it is needed
  - **Always:** Name the outgoing and incoming anchor of every seam

## Craft-quality expectations

### R-AST-001 — Generated imagery names a specific subject, setting and detail tied to a beat; product UI is captured, never generated; logos are supplied.

- **Check:** tool `assets:check_plan`; rubric dimensions: DES-SPECIFICITY, ACC-UI
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_asset_plan_rules`

### R-MOT-001 — Explanatory illustrations become animation that clarifies the problem; a static plate with a pan is not an explanation.

- **Check:** reviewer cases; rubric dimensions: CRE-MOTION
- **Default:** enforced
  - **Never:** Use a still illustration with only a camera move for an explanatory beat
  - **Always:** Animate the causal elements in the order the narration names them

### R-ACC-004 — Real UI pixels stay untouched: veils, blurs and camera moves are verified by a pixel-integrity audit with negative controls, and never mirror or reveal cut-off content.

- **Check:** reviewer cases; rubric dimensions: ACC-UI
- **Default:** advisory
  - **Never:** A backdrop-filter veil over product UI
  - **Never:** Readable cut-off words at a veil edge
  - **Always:** Compare rendered product pixels with the capture
  - **Always:** Prove the audit can fail (negative controls)

### R-UI-001 — Camera crops land in empty gutters, never through product text.

- **Check:** reviewer cases; rubric dimensions: CRE-POLISH
- **Default:** advisory
  - **Never:** Crop through a label or a paragraph at the frame edge
  - **Always:** Choose zooms whose edges fall in layout gutters

### R-UI-002 — Focus rings and highlights hold ≥ 1 s and never rest mid-slide over a label.

- **Check:** tool `legibility:check (rings)`; rubric dimensions: LEG-RING
- **Default:** advisory
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_legibility_flags_small_low_contrast_short_ghost`

### R-REG-005 — When a baseline master is configured, creative review must compare baseline-vs-candidate strips and confirm no beat is worse.

- **Check:** reviewer cases; rubric dimensions: REG-VERDICT
- **Default:** advisory
- **Threshold:** review score ≥ 4 when applicable
  - **Never:** score the candidate without baseline comparison
  - **Always:** cite strip frames

## Legibility and accessibility

### R-CAP-001 — Captions are speech-locked: never after the first spoken word; mid-sentence lead ≤ 0.20 s; sentence-first lead ≤ 0.45 s into cleared time; never clear &gt; 0.10 s before the last word.

- **Check:** tool `captions:sync`; rubric dimensions: ACC-CAPTIONS
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_caption_sync_detects_lag_and_early_clear`

### R-CAP-002 — Caption reading rate ≤ 20 characters/s and each cue ≥ 0.8 s.

- **Check:** tool `captions:sync`; rubric dimensions: ACC-CAPTIONS
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_caption_sync_detects_lag_and_early_clear`

### R-LEG-001 — Critical text is ≥ 22 px at 1080p.

- **Check:** tool `legibility:check`; rubric dimensions: LEG-SIZE
- **Default:** enforced
- **Threshold:** 22 px
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_legibility_flags_small_low_contrast_short_ghost`

### R-LEG-002 — Text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 (≥ 3:1 for large text), using only approved text/background pairs.

- **Check:** tool `legibility:check`; rubric dimensions: LEG-CONTRAST
- **Default:** enforced
- **Threshold:** WCAG 1.4.3
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_legibility_flags_small_low_contrast_short_ghost`

### R-LEG-003 — Every text is on screen at least max(1.0 s, 0.24 s × words).

- **Check:** tool `legibility:check`; rubric dimensions: LEG-DWELL, PAC-READ
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_legibility_flags_small_low_contrast_short_ghost`

### R-LEG-004 — Essential content stays inside the title-safe area (x 96–1824 at 1920 wide).

- **Check:** tool `legibility:check`; rubric dimensions: LEG-SAFE
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_legibility_flags_small_low_contrast_short_ghost`

### R-LEG-005 — Nothing essential sits in the caption band (below y 900) while captions are on.

- **Check:** tool `legibility:check`; rubric dimensions: LEG-SAFE
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_legibility_flags_small_low_contrast_short_ghost`

### R-LEG-006 — No ghost text: de-emphasised text steps down to a solid grey token, never partial opacity.

- **Check:** tool `legibility:check`; rubric dimensions: LEG-GHOST
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_legibility_flags_small_low_contrast_short_ghost`

### R-LEG-007 — No more than 3 flashes in any second; colour is never the only carrier of meaning.

- **Check:** tool `legibility:check`; rubric dimensions: LEG-FLASH, LEG-COLOR-CUE
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_flash_detection`

### R-LAY-001 — No text, chip or card may overlap another, and no line may run through text in the rendered layout.

- **Check:** tool `layout:check`; rubric dimensions: LEG-OVERLAP
- **Default:** advisory
- **Threshold:** zero TEXT_OVERLAP, BOX_OVERLAP or LINE_THROUGH_TEXT runs
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_b3_regression_harness.py::test_layout_rows_from_synthetic_audit_and_not_measured`

### R-LAY-002 — Held text may not be clipped by its mask, viewport or panel.

- **Check:** tool `layout:check`; rubric dimensions: LEG-CLIP
- **Default:** advisory
- **Threshold:** zero TEXT_CLIPPED runs
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_b3_regression_harness.py::test_layout_rows_from_synthetic_audit_and_not_measured`

### R-LAY-003 — Text and text-bearing panels stay inside the stage; off-frame zooms are regressions.

- **Check:** tool `layout:check`; rubric dimensions: LEG-OFFSTAGE
- **Default:** advisory
- **Threshold:** zero OFFSTAGE runs
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_b3_regression_harness.py::test_layout_rows_from_synthetic_audit_and_not_measured`

### R-CAP-003 — Captions must contain the same words as the approved script after normalization; missing caption words are accessibility regressions.

- **Check:** tool `layout:check_caption_script`; rubric dimensions: CAP-SCRIPT
- **Default:** advisory
- **Threshold:** zero missing or extra caption words
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_b3_regression_harness.py::test_caption_script_exact_match_and_missing_word`

## Visual consistency and detail

### R-DES-002 — Typography is one system: section titles, infographics and the bookends share the same families in defined roles.

- **Check:** tool `design:compliance`; rubric dimensions: DES-TYPE, DES-CONSISTENCY
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_design_compliance_flags_font_logo_palette`

### R-DES-005 — Every drawn colour and font traces to design.md tokens (the design-compliance trace replaces 'it doesn't follow design.md').

- **Check:** tool `design:compliance`; rubric dimensions: DES-TOKENS
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_design_compliance_flags_font_logo_palette`

### R-LAY-004 — A panel may not sit empty after its title appears; empty-tier holds are regressions.

- **Check:** tool `layout:check`; rubric dimensions: LEG-EMPTY
- **Default:** advisory
- **Threshold:** zero EMPTY_PANEL runs
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_b3_regression_harness.py::test_layout_rows_from_synthetic_audit_and_not_measured`

## Voice, sound, tone, pacing and transitions

### R-VOI-001 — Narration matches the project's approved voice profile and delivery; listening quality is judged by a named human.

- **Check:** a named human decides; rubric dimensions: VOI-ADULT
- **Default:** enforced
  - **Never:** Ship a delivery that contradicts the approved voice direction
  - **Always:** Record the project-selected voice profile and delivery in voice-direction.json
  - **Always:** Request the project owner's listening sign-off
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_voice_direction_matches_the_project_profile`

### R-VOI-002 — No stutter, dropped word, clipped ending or seam: every script unit is spoken in order, and mixing never attenuates inside speech by more than a 6 dB breath dip.

- **Check:** tool `audio:check_voice`; rubric dimensions: VOI-COMPLETE
- **Default:** enforced
- **Threshold:** max_speech_dip_db 6
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_voice_check_catches_dropped_unit`

### R-VOI-003 — Pronunciation is verified per product term; if a term is misheard in most takes, rephrase the line instead of shipping the error.

- **Check:** reviewer cases; rubric dimensions: VOI-PRONUNCIATION
- **Default:** enforced
  - **Never:** Keep a product term that ASR mishears in most takes
  - **Always:** List product terms and their expected pronunciation in voice-direction.json

### R-AUD-001 — Deliver at −16 LUFS integrated (±1) with true peak ≤ −1 dBTP, measured on the encoded master.

- **Check:** tool `media:technical_qa`; rubric dimensions: TEC-LOUDNESS
- **Default:** enforced
- **Threshold:** -16 LUFS ±1; TP ≤ -1 dBTP
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_technical_qa_on_real_media`

### R-AUD-002 — Music supports the voice: look-ahead ducking under speech, no competing phrases, no abrupt cuts; voice over music p10 ≥ 16 LU.

- **Check:** a named human decides; rubric dimensions: CRE-MUSIC
- **Default:** enforced
  - **Never:** Let music phrases compete with narration
  - **Never:** Cut music abruptly at a seam
  - **Always:** Duck under speech
  - **Always:** Test several directions before choosing

### R-AUD-003 — Every silence longer than 1.5 s is a planned pause; unexplained silence is a defect.

- **Check:** tool `media:technical_qa`; rubric dimensions: TEC-SILENCE
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_technical_qa_flags_unexplained_silence`

### R-MOT-002 — Motion and transitions serve comprehension: one brand-derived vocabulary, motivated seams (line-carry, matched frames), no decorative or repetitive transitions.

- **Check:** reviewer cases; rubric dimensions: CRE-TRANSITIONS, NAR-CONNECTION
- **Default:** enforced
  - **Never:** A transition that doesn't advance the story
  - **Never:** A new effect on every cut
  - **Always:** One transition per seam, specified in the storyboard

### R-VOI-004 — Narration seams must be silent and continuous: no hard cuts, loud tails into the next unit, overlaps or hard onsets.

- **Check:** tool `audio:check_seams`; rubric dimensions: VOI-SEAMS
- **Default:** advisory
- **Threshold:** see config/defaults.yaml thresholds.audio.seams
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_b3_regression_harness.py::test_voice_seams_clean_hard_cut_loud_tail_and_overlap`

## Storytelling and product demonstrations

### R-ACC-001 — The engineers' terminology is the source of truth: never invent a term, and map requested terms that have no source instead of adopting them.

- **Check:** tool `accuracy:check_script`; rubric dimensions: ACC-TERMS, ACC-CLAIMS
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_accuracy_flags_prohibited_and_unverified`

### R-ACC-002 — No invented UI, metrics, counters, claims or architecture edges; the prototype is shown untouched, with boundary tags where the demo is synthetic or target-state.

- **Check:** tool `accuracy:check_film`; rubric dimensions: ACC-UI, ACC-BOUNDARIES
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_accuracy_flags_generated_ui`

### R-ACC-003 — Demonstrate the interactions required by the approved brief, using source-supported detail rather than unsupported claims.

- **Check:** reviewer cases; rubric dimensions: ACC-DEPTH
- **Default:** enforced
  - **Never:** Omit an interaction required by the approved brief
  - **Never:** Describe a feature without showing it
  - **Always:** Show the required interaction and its source-supported result

### R-UI-003 — Direct attention to real UI with highlight rings on measured boxes and restrained camera moves (video-shotcraft), so the viewer knows where to look.

- **Check:** reviewer cases; rubric dimensions: CRE-FOCUS
- **Default:** enforced
  - **Never:** Show a full screen with no focus cue
  - **Always:** Ring the element the narration names

## Recurring failure patterns

### R-PRO-002 — Machine QA and critic READY are never human approval: human listening, taste and release are separate named decisions, and dry-run approvals are labelled not human.

- **Check:** tool `engine:decide`; rubric dimensions: none
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_engine.py::test_human_gate_requires_named_human`

### R-PRO-007 — Every version is reviewed on its own rendered evidence by an independent critic through the project's review lenses; an earlier READY never survives new rejection.

- **Check:** tool `evaluation:gate (reviews must be current-version)`; rubric dimensions: CRE-LENSES
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_engine.py::test_gate_blocks_without_current_reviews`

### R-REG-001 — Compare each candidate with the released baseline; undeclared removals, content loss and demo regressions fail the gate.

- **Check:** tool `regress:check`; rubric dimensions: REG-BASELINE
- **Default:** advisory
- **Threshold:** content_retained ≥ 0.7; demo metrics within configured thresholds
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_b3_regression_harness.py::test_regression_baseline_detects_removals_departures_scope_and_content_loss`

## Effective corrective actions

### R-PRO-003 — Freeze and hash the source evidence before rendering; if sources drift, re-render from the frozen sources instead of weakening the test.

- **Check:** tool `engine:_integrity_problems`; rubric dimensions: none
- **Default:** advisory
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_engine.py::test_frozen_inputs_are_immutable`

### R-PRO-008 — Scope each rework to the exact critic findings and re-run only what they trace to; never restart broadly.

- **Check:** tool `regen:plan`; rubric dimensions: none
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_engine.py::test_targeted_rework_cycle`

### R-PRO-009 — Resume from durable project state (state, checkpoints, ledger, repo files), never from a long chat history; preserve the original session.

- **Check:** tool `engine:_resume_fixups`; rubric dimensions: none
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_engine.py::test_resume_does_not_rerun_approved`

### R-PRO-010 — A correction must produce fresh evidence: a defect resolves only when its reviewer re-runs on a newer version and no longer reports it; a fix that changes nothing counts as a failed attempt.

- **Check:** tool `evaluation:compare_after_rework`; rubric dimensions: none
- **Default:** inactive
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_engine.py::test_fix_that_changes_nothing_is_not_resolved`

## Production practices that are defaults

### R-PRO-001 — Never stop after one production round: keep the produce→critique→fix loop running until every gate passes or a genuine blocker is reported.

- **Check:** tool `engine:review_gate`; rubric dimensions: none
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_engine.py::test_targeted_rework_cycle`

### R-PRO-004 — Prove a change on one 10–15 s clip with real assets before batching it across the film.

- **Check:** reviewer cases; rubric dimensions: none
- **Default:** enforced
  - **Never:** Batch a new look, voice or motion rule across every chapter before a single-clip proof
  - **Always:** Render a 10–15 s actual-asset proof and review it first

### R-PRO-005 — Preserve every rejected version with its failure evidence; replace a strong element only when the new one is demonstrably better.

- **Check:** tool `engine:_commit_outputs (superseded, never deleted)`; rubric dimensions: none
- **Default:** enforced
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_engine.py::test_lineage_and_superseded_artifacts`

### R-PRO-006 — The runtime cap is a hard constraint: cut words and holds, never evidence the viewer needs, and never speed up the voice.

- **Check:** tool `pacing:estimate_script`; rubric dimensions: PAC-RUNTIME, TEC-DURATION
- **Default:** enforced
- **Threshold:** brief.runtime_max_s
- **Synthetic regression:** `tests/test_tools.py::test_runtime_estimate_blocks_over_cap`
